title: Self-host daemon rebuilds itself: drain, build, swap, restart
lead: Owner decision (2026-11-18, adj 464 `selfhost.auto-rebuild`, supersedes adj 232): for a self-host project that opts in, the daemon rebuilds and restarts itself after a landing that leaves it behind main. It drains first: no new role starts, running roles finish and are never killed, then it builds, validates, swaps the binary and restarts, and held runs resume.
findings_note: 2026-11-18: after S332, S403, S405 and S404 landed, the daemon stayed on build 7f5a1f7d, so landed fixes (the changelog-entry gate, ork wait, the tracking commit) did not apply to new runs. `ork daemon restart --rebuild` refuses while any role runs, even with --force (`docs/design.md:3847-3849`, adj 312), and with three runs in flight there was no gap; the orchestrator retried it every 30 s from a shell loop. The rebuild runs in the CLI (`internal/cli/lifecycle.go:88-120`); the daemon only reports behind main (`internal/daemon/build.go:25`, `:173`).

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: A daemon behind main runs old code, so every landed engine fix waits for a hand restart that can only happen when no role runs. Under a full slot cap that gap rarely comes on its own. Draining bounds the wait to one role's length. Owner rule (2026-11-17): regular, deterministic steps are code.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `TestAutoRebuildDrainsThenRestarts` in `internal/daemon/build_test.go`: a self-host project with `auto_rebuild` on and a fake build command; after a landing leaves the daemon behind main, a role that is running finishes, no new role starts meanwhile, then the build runs once and the restart path is called once.
- `TestAutoRebuildHoldsNewRoles` in `internal/daemon/runs_test.go`: while draining, a run that reaches a role start waits with reason "waiting for daemon rebuild" and starts that role after the restart.
- `TestAutoRebuildFailedBuildReleasesHold` in `internal/daemon/build_test.go`: the build exits 1; the old daemon keeps running, the hold is released, held runs continue on the old build, and status carries the last output lines and "daemon not rebuilt".
- `TestAutoRebuildOffKeepsManual` in `internal/daemon/build_test.go`: with `auto_rebuild` off (the default) nothing is held or built; the behind notice is unchanged.
- `TestAutoRebuildNeverKillsARole` in `internal/daemon/build_test.go`: no code path in the drain cancels a running role.
- Also added: `TestAutoRebuildHoldsAStartQueuedForASlot`, `TestAutoRebuildRunStartsTheSuccessor`, `TestAutoRebuildUnchangedBuildKeepsTheDaemon` and `TestExecutableRevisionReadsThisProcess` (build_test.go), `TestProjectsSetAutoRebuildRules` and `TestRebuildNotice` (rebuild_test.go), `TestRunBuild` (build_test.go), `TestHold*` and `TestSpecRoleWaitsForTheHold` (engine/hold_test.go), `TestProjectsSetAutoRebuild*`, `TestUsageTextNamesProjectsSetAutoRebuild` and `TestStatusPrintsTheDaemonRebuild` (cli_test.go), `TestStatusLineShowsTheRebuild`, `TestHeldRunShowsTheRebuildWait` and the auto-rebuild case of `TestLandedRebuildNotice` (tui/rebuild_test.go).

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the failing tests above and see them red for the stated reason.
2. Registry: `auto_rebuild` bool, default off, only allowed with a non-empty `build_command` on a self-host project; `ork projects set NAME --auto-rebuild on|off`.
3. Daemon: after a landing (and at start) when the project is self-host, behind main, opted in and has a build command, enter draining: hold every new role start (engine and spec-check roles), let running roles end.
4. When no role runs: build through the same code the CLI uses (shared helper, ten-minute timeout, process-group cleanup), into the installed path the build command writes; validate the executable as the CLI restart does; then stop and restart the daemon through the existing path. Runs resume through today's restart recovery.
5. A failed build: keep the old daemon, release the hold, record the failure in status (last twenty lines), and do not retry until main moves again.
6. Status, `ork status` and the TUI status line show "rebuild pending: waiting for N roles" while draining and the held runs' reason.
7. Docs: `docs/design.md` self-host rebuild section (adj 464 supersedes adj 232; "There is no automatic rebuild" becomes the opt-in drain) and `docs/guide.md` troubleshooting rows. Changelog entry with `slicer changelog add`.

Owner decisions (2026-11-18): How does the daemon restart itself after the build, when the existing restart path is driven by the CLI? -> successor: before exiting, the daemon starts `ork daemon run` from the newly built executable, detached, with the same validation and start code the CLI uses (`cmd/ork/start.go:48-90`, `prepareDaemonRestartExe`). It moves that code to a place the daemon can call, and the new daemon takes over the lock and recovers runs. [selfhost.auto-rebuild-restart].

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
Acceptance criteria:
- With auto_rebuild on, a landing that leaves the self-host daemon behind main ends with the daemon on the new build without any hand command, and no role was killed.
- While draining, no new role starts and status says why.
- A failed build leaves the old daemon running, releases held runs and reports the build output.
- With auto_rebuild off, behaviour is unchanged.

Commands:
- `go test ./internal/daemon -run 'TestAutoRebuild' -v`
- `go vet ./...`
- `go test ./...`
- `gofmt -l .` must print nothing.
- [HUMAN CHECK] With `ork projects set ork --auto-rebuild on`, land a slice that changes internal/engine while another run is implementing; the daemon restarts on the new build after that role ends.
